text_blocks.snippet: Common side effects of losartan include dizziness, cold-like symptoms, and fatigue, which are generally mild and often improve as your body adjusts to the medication.
You can read more comprehensive details on the GoodRx Losartan Guide or check the NHS Losartan Overview.
These symptoms usually do not require emergency care and often fade after a few weeks:

list.snippet: Dizziness or lightheadedness: Often happens when standing up too quickly because your blood pressure has dropped.
Cold symptoms: A stuffy nose, sinus pain, or upper respiratory tract infection.
Fatigue: Feeling more tired or weak than usual.
Pain: Back pain, leg pain, or mild muscle and joint aches.
Digestive issues: Mild nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or indigestion.
Headaches: Mild head pain when starting the drug.

text_blocks.snippet: Consult a doctor or seek immediate medical help if you experience severe or dangerous issues, as detailed by MedlinePlus and the Mayo Clinic:

list.snippet: Allergic reaction (Angioedema): Sudden swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing. Get emergency help right away.
High potassium levels (Hyperkalemia): Can cause muscle weakness, numbness, or an irregular heartbeat. Often has no symptoms, so routine blood tests are necessary.
Low blood pressure (Hypotension): Causes severe dizziness, confusion, blurred vision, or fainting.
Kidney problems: Changes in how much you urinate, dark urine, or swelling in your hands, feet, and ankles.
Pregnancy risk: Do not take losartan if you are pregnant, as it can cause serious harm or birth defects to an unborn baby.
